Hin Lad is a jungle waterfall 2–3 km inland from Nathon on Koh Samui's west side, reached on foot from a trailhead beside a forest temple, Wat Namtok Hin Lad. The path climbs a stream valley past several small tiers and pools; the walk between tiers takes 30–45 minutes on steep, uneven ground, so allow about two hours in total. No official fee or opening hours are published (go in daylight; a donation box is reported). Flow is best October–January and low February–April.

Map

Hin Lad lies on the western slope of the island's central ridge, south-east of Nathon town and 3 km from Lipa Noi. It is the opposite side of the ridge from Na Muang, about 7 km away as the crow flies but 30–35 minutes by road.

[kp_places_map type="waterfall" title="Hin Lad and Samui's other waterfalls"]

The trail

Hin Lad is a series of small cascades rather than one big drop. The appeal is the walk: shaded forest, a clear stream and very few people compared with Na Muang. Reviewers describe the path as well kept and shaded in the lower section, then steeper and rougher above.

  1. 0 min Park near the trailhead by the temple grounds. Put on proper shoes and fill your water bottles; there is nothing further up.
  2. 5 min Walk past the temple area quietly and follow the path upstream into the forest. The first, lowest tier and pool come quickly.
  3. 5–45 min The trail climbs over roots, rock steps and loose stones beside the stream to the next tiers. Expect 30–45 minutes between the lower and upper sections.
  4. Top Small pools under the upper cascades: a good place to cool off and rest in the shade.
  5. Return Come back the same way; allow as long as the climb. Take extra care on the steep sections going down.

The number of tiers you reach depends on how far up you go and on the season; in the dry months the upper falls can be little more than wet rock. If you only have 20 minutes, the lowest tier is close to the trailhead, but it is the walk further up that makes the trip worthwhile.

The forest temple and etiquette

The trail starts by Wat Namtok Hin Lad, a forest monastery (the name means "Hin Lad Waterfall Temple"). Forest temples in Thailand are places for meditation, so behave as you would in any active temple:

  • Cover shoulders and knees near the temple buildings; carry a sarong or light shirt to slip on over swimwear.
  • Keep voices low and music off.
  • Take your shoes off before entering any hall, and don't point your feet at Buddha images or monks.
  • Women should not touch monks or hand things to them directly.
  • Drop a small donation in the box if you use the trail; 20–50 THB is a reasonable amount.

Our guide to Thai culture and traditions explains temple etiquette in more detail, and Koh Samui temples lists the other wats worth visiting.

When it has water

Like all of Samui's falls, Hin Lad depends on the north-east monsoon, which brings most of the year's rain from October to December.

October–December263–445 mm a monthStrongest flow; muddy, slippery path; flash floods after downpours
January127 mmGood flow and drier paths: the best month
February–April64–116 mmLow; upper tiers may be a trickle
May–September102–134 mmModerate after showers

If you are staying in Nathon, Lipa Noi or Taling Ngam, Hin Lad is the obvious choice. From Chaweng or Lamai, Na Muang is closer and easier. Compare all three on our waterfalls hub.

Is Hin Lad worth it?

Our honest verdict: Hin Lad is worth a morning if you are staying on the west or north-west coast, you like walking, and it is between October and January. You get a shaded forest path, a clear stream, small cool pools and far fewer people than at Na Muang. It is not worth crossing the island from Chaweng for, and from February to April the upper tiers can be little more than wet rock, so lower your expectations or go to Na Muang 1 for a swim instead.

Some visitors see only the lowest tier in 10 minutes and leave unimpressed. The point of Hin Lad is the walk up the valley: give it the full two hours or skip it.

A west-side morning

  1. 08:00 Coffee in Nathon, then drive 5–10 minutes inland to the trailhead.
  2. 08:30 Start the walk while the valley is cool and quiet.
  3. 09:30 Swim in the upper pools and rest in the shade.
  4. 10:30 Back at the trailhead; leave a donation in the box.
  5. 11:00 Lunch in Nathon: noodle shops and the old Chinese shophouses along the seafront roads.
  6. 14:00 Swim at Lipa Noi at high tide, then the sunset from Nathon pier or Taling Ngam.

Safety

  • Slippery ground: wet roots and rocks are the main hazard. Go slowly, especially downhill, and don't climb on the rocks beside the cascades.
  • Flash floods: after heavy rain, especially October–December, the stream can rise quickly. If the water rises or turns brown, move away from the stream bed.
  • Tell someone: the valley is quiet and mobile signal is patchy. Let your hotel know where you are going and when you expect to be back.
  • Heat and water: carry at least 1.5–2 litres per person.
  • Mosquitoes: dengue is present in Thailand year-round; wear repellent.
  • Emergency: ambulance 1669, Tourist Police 1155. The government Koh Samui Hospital is on the outskirts of Nathon; see hospitals.

Getting there

From Nathon, head inland (south-east) and follow the signs for Hin Lad Waterfall; the access road is in good condition and fine for a scooter. There is no songthaew service to the trailhead.

Taxis are easiest to find in Nathon town; agree a return fare with waiting time. Grab coverage on the west coast is weak. Rental tips: motorbike rental, car rental and getting around.

If you are coming from the east coast, pair Hin Lad with a long lunch in Nathon and stay on the west side for the sunset, rather than driving back across the island in the midday traffic.

What to bring

  • Closed shoes or strapped sports sandals with grip
  • 1.5–2 litres of water and a snack
  • Swimwear and a small towel
  • A sarong or shirt for the temple grounds
  • Insect repellent and sunscreen
  • Small notes for the donation box

Boat trips from the west coast

Staying near Nathon? The Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB adult, 1,250 THB child) leaves from Thong Krut on the south-west coast and runs every day. For a bigger day out, the Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan day trip costs 2,200 THB adult and 1,600 THB child. Hotel transfers are included from the main areas; Nathon is a remote area for Chaweng-side departures, at +400 THB per person return.
